title: Throttle Control Sprint — Lightning Ops Log
body:
Meeting: Throttle Control Sprint — Lightning Ops (Wed 2025-02-12)
Time: 09:00–09:45 PT
Location: Zoom + #release-ops Slack thread
Attendees: Asha (owner), Marco, Erin, Liam, Nina, David K. (oncall), SRE rotation (Sam)
Absentees: none

Purpose and context:
- Rapid coordination for a recurring inter-region throttle misconfiguration that surfaced in the last 48h. Several customer requests hit the burst pool and triggered a throttle policy which then backfilled requests into the hosted fallback causing elevated p95 on token generation. This sprint is to: 1) triage root cause, 2) land short-term mitigations for the next 72h, 3) schedule safe roll-forward/rollback tests and a rehearsal.

High-level summary:
- Incident: partial degradation in hosted API for a subset of customers using Dedicated-burst routing; symptom was token emission stalls (~300–700ms additional p95) for sequences >512 tokens.
- Cause hypothesis: mis-applied throttle multiplier in autoscale policy PR merged yesterday (runtime autoscaler change) combined with a stale routing override (customer-level routing pinned to burst pool).
- Impact: 2 customers (account IDs redacted in notes) experienced degraded throughput for long-running generation jobs (~6% of overall tail traffic). No data breach, no model corruption.
- Detection: Synthetic-runner alerts + SLO slack monitor at 03:12 UTC; first user report at 03:20 UTC.

Timeline (local times rounded):
- 02:50 UTC: synthetic runner p95 spike (alerts)
- 03:05 UTC: Ops receives user report -> Pager -> David K. tries repro
- 03:18 UTC: Quick triage shows increase in queue length on burst pool nodes
- 03:25 UTC: Canary routing fallback engaged automatically for new requests (policy Fallback-1)
- 03:40 UTC: Manual temporary throttle cap applied by SRE to burst pool (cap reduced from 1.5x -> 1.1x) to reduce queuing
- 04:10 UTC: Hotfix PR opened to revert autoscaler multiplier change (see PR #2418)
- 04:28 UTC: PR tested in canary region (eu-west-1-canary) with synthetic load — baseline restored
- 04:45 UTC: Manual rollout of PR to primary regions; continued monitoring

Short-term mitigations (actionable items already executed):
- Reverted recent autoscaler multiplier change (runtime PR landed: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2418). Owner: Marco — merged and rolled to canary at 04:28 UTC.
- Applied conservative throttle cap to burst pool to prevent runaway queueing. Owner: Sam (SRE) — cap set and annotated in infra dashboard.
- Temporarily widened canary traffic window from 5% -> 12% for this patch to validate under realistic mix. Owner: Nina.
- Engaged CS to notify affected customers and provide ETA. Owner: Erin.

Decisions and rationale:
- Rollback-first stance: since the change was small and recent, decision was to revert autoscaler multiplier rather than attempt surgical tuning in prod. Rationale: fastest path to restore stable p95.
- Keep throttle cap in place for 72 hours to observe traffic patterns across weekday/weekend mix. Rationale: autoscaler oscillations can take time to surface.
- Do not modify routing overrides for customers until we complete explicit audit of pinned overrides. Rationale: avoid unexpected customer impact; audit scheduled.

Follow-up work (owners and target dates):
1) Full audit of routing overrides that pin customers to burst pool (JIRA-RE-9823). Owner: Marco. Due: 2025-02-18.
2) Add safety gate to autoscaler PRs that simulates steady-state traffic + long-sequence jobs in CI. Owner: Liam. Due: 2025-02-20.
3) Create a small e2e test in the integration suite that reproduces queueing when throttle multiplier >1.2. Owner: Asha + Marco. Due: 2025-02-17.
4) Update throttle-control playbook with explicit rollback checklist and Slack runbook links. Owner: Nina. Due: 2025-02-14 (draft), 2025-02-21 (final).
5) Customer follow-up package: timeline, root cause note, mitigations, and credits. Owner: Erin (CS). Due: 2025-02-15.
6) Postmortem doc with metrics slice, flamegraphs, and kernel-selection trace. Owner: David K. + SRE. Due: 2025-02-19.

Risk assessment and mitigations for next 7 days:
- Risk: repeated autoscaler changes without realistic long-sequence tests. Mitigation: CI safety gate (see #2).
- Risk: hidden pinned routes remain and amplify localized load. Mitigation: routing audit + temporary rate-limits per-pinned-customer during high load windows.
- Risk: rollback may reintroduce previous autoscaling behavior that was intentionally changed for a good reason. Mitigation: gather telemetry on what problem the original change attempted to solve and propose a canary-safe redesign.

Testing plan for roll-forward (if we need to reapply change):
- Create dedicated canary bucket with 20%-traffic and synthetic long-seq generation run every 10m for 48h.
- Monitor token/sec, p50/p95 latency, queue depth, and autoscaler decision logs.
- Gate requires no >5% regression in p95 over baseline and no queue depth > 3 nodes sustained for >5m.
- Use automated rollback hook if gate violated. Owner for orchestration: Liam.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did the autoscaler multiplier change combine with the routing override to produce a nonlinear queueing effect? Hypothesis: multiplier increased target utilization which reduced spare capacity during long sequences; pinned routes prevented dynamic rebalancing. Needs kernel-level trace.
- Should we require a minimal canary duration for infra changes that touch autoscaler logic? Proposal: yes — add a 48h canary rule. To be discussed in next infra retro.

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- This doc is deliberately brief; more detailed data (logs, flamegraphs, heap dumps) will be linked into the postmortem.
- If you review linked PR #2418, look at autoscaler config delta and the unit test coverage. We missed synthetic long-seq tests.

Immediate next steps (next 24h):
- Marco: complete routing override audit kickoff and post first findings.
- Liam: spec CI safety gate and start a spike for long-seq synthetic runner.
- Nina: update playbook draft and add checklist entries for throttle cap and rollback.
- Erin: finalize customer notice and send to ops-legal review.
- David K./SRE: keep throttle cap and watch the histogram dashboards; escalate if p95 rises >3% above baseline.

Appendix (quick links):
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2418
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RE-9823
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02RELEASE/p1678901234567890
- Playbook (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RE/pages/3456789/throttle-control-playbook

End of notes.

Quick snapshot of metrics at 09:00 PT (post-rollback, sanity check):
- Global p95 tokens: baseline +0.8% (within expected noise)
- Burst pool queue depth: returned to baseline levels
- Canary traffic success: 100% without violation

If anything regresses overnight, escalate to oncall and convene a fast-follow standup.
